content:
Let the Ann patches in the 10 rows, from south to north, have row lengths
\[
a_1\ge a_2\ge \cdots \ge a_{10}.
\]
The closure condition gives this nonincreasing sequence, and
\[
a_1+\cdots+a_{10}=30.
\]

A scarecrow occurs exactly when a row length drops from some positive height less than 10:
\[
a_i>a_{i+1},\qquad 1\le a_i<10.
\]
So each scarecrow corresponds to a distinct positive starting height. If there are \(k\) scarecrows, these \(k\) heights are distinct positive integers, so the total number of Ann patches is at least
\[
1+2+\cdots+k=\frac{k(k+1)}2.
\]
Since Ann farms 30 patches,
\[
\frac{k(k+1)}2\le 30.
\]
Thus \(k\le 7\), because \(8\cdot 9/2=36>30\).

This is achievable with row lengths
\[
9,6,5,4,3,2,1,0,0,0,
\]
which sum to \(30\) and have exactly \(7\) counted drops.

\[
\boxed{7}
\]
